name: Inkjet Printing-Based Volumetric Display
definition: A volumetric display constructed by printing photoreactive luminescence materials (fluorescent inks) onto multiple layers of transparent films using a commercial inkjet printer, which are then stacked to form a 3D volume. The volume elements (voxels) are excited by external light (e.g., UV) to emit light, forming a 3D image.
summary: Inkjet printing-based volumetric displays create physical 3D images by stacking transparent films printed with fluorescent inks, differing from other methods by using pre-printed static layers rather than dynamic optical addressing.
